desc:
For every index i of text, compute the length of the longest prefix of pattern that appears in text starting exactly at i. In other words, the length of the longest common prefix of pattern and text[i..]. Return an array with one entry per position of text.

Example: pattern = "aab" and text = "aabaaab" give [3,1,0,2,3,1,0]. At index 3 the text continues with "aaab", which shares only "aa" with the pattern, so the value is 2.
constraints: Both strings consist of lowercase English letters
hints: Extending each position character by character is O(n · m) in the worst case (think "aaaa..."). You need to reuse earlier work.
The Z-function of a string gives, at each index, the longest common prefix with the whole string. Can you turn the pattern and the text into one string?
Compute the Z-function of pattern + '#' + text (the separator is not a lowercase letter, so matches never run past the pattern). The values after the separator are the answers.
editorial: Concatenate pattern, a separator that cannot occur in the input such as '#', and text. The Z-function z[j] is the length of the longest common prefix of the concatenation and its suffix starting at j. For positions inside the text part, that prefix is a prefix of the pattern, and it is automatically capped at m by the separator.

So the answer for text index i is z[m + 1 + i]. The Z-algorithm keeps a window [l, r) that matches the string's prefix; positions inside the window start from the already known value z[j - l] (capped by the window end) and extend only beyond the window, which gives linear total work.

Time O(n + m) and space O(n + m). The result is also the 'matching statistics against a prefix' that KMP implicitly computes, but with the Z-function it is available for every position, not only where the match is maximal.
